From: Sam Sun <samsun1006219@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2024 14:55:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bonding: Fix out-of-bounds read in
 bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set()

In function bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set(), if newval->string is an
empty string, newval->string+1 will point to the byte after the
string, causing an out-of-bound read.

diff --git a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_options.c b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_options.c
index 0cacd7027e35..bc80fb6397dc 100644
--- a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_options.c
+++ b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_options.c
@@ -1214,9 +1214,9 @@ static int bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set(struct bonding *bond,
 	__be32 target;
 
 	if (newval->string) {
-		if (!in4_pton(newval->string+1, -1, (u8 *)&target, -1, NULL)) {
-			netdev_err(bond->dev, "invalid ARP target %pI4 specified\n",
-				   &target);
+		if (strlen(newval->string) < 1 ||
+		    !in4_pton(newval->string + 1, -1, (u8 *)&target, -1, NULL)) {
+			netdev_err(bond->dev, "invalid ARP target specified\n");
 			return ret;
 		}
 		if (newval->string[0] == '+')
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/bonding/bond_options.c`**
   - The function `bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set` was modified to include a check for the length of `newval->string`. 
   - The original code attempted to access `newval->string + 1` without verifying if `newval->string` was empty, which could lead to an out-of-bounds read.
   - The new code adds a condition to check if the length of `newval->string` is less than 1 before proceeding with the `in4_pton` function call. If the string is empty, it logs an error message and returns early.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bond_options.c` directly addresses the bug report regarding an out-of-bounds read caused by accessing memory beyond the allocated string when it is empty. 
- By adding a length check before dereferencing the string, the patch prevents the potential crash or undefined behavior that could occur when the function attempts to read from an invalid memory location. This change enhances the robustness of the code and ensures that the function behaves correctly even when provided with invalid input.

Fix it by adding a check of string length before using it.

Fixes: f9de11a16594 ("bonding: add ip checks when store ip target")
Signed-off-by: Yue Sun <samsun1006219@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Jay Vosburgh <jay.vosburgh@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Hangbin Liu <liuhangbin@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20240702-bond-oob-v6-1-2dfdba195c19@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the function `bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set` attempting to access `newval->string + 1` without checking if `newval->string` is an empty string. This results in an out-of-bounds read, as it tries to read memory beyond the allocated space for the string when it is empty, leading to potential crashes or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int bond_option_arp_ip_targets_set(struct bonding *bond,
 					  const struct bond_opt_value *newval)
 {
 	int ret = -EPERM;
 	__be32 target;
 
 	if (newval->string) {
-		if (!in4_pton(newval->string+1, -1, (u8 *)&target, -1, NULL)) {
-			netdev_err(bond->dev, "invalid ARP target %pI4 specified\n",
-				   &target);
+		if (strlen(newval->string) < 1 ||
+		    !in4_pton(newval->string + 1, -1, (u8 *)&target, -1, NULL)) {
+			netdev_err(bond->dev, "invalid ARP target specified\n");
 			return ret;
 		}
 		if (newval->string[0] == '+')
 			ret = bond_option_arp_ip_target_add(bond, target);
 		else if (newval->string[0] == '-')
 			ret = bond_option_arp_ip_target_rem(bond, target);
 		else
 			netdev_err(bond->dev, "no command found in arp_ip_targets file - use +<addr> or -<addr>\n");
 	} else {
 		target = newval->value;
 		ret = bond_option_arp_ip_target_add(bond, target);
 	}
 
 	return ret;
 }
